must_fit.reason: If it does not fit the shelf it will live somewhere else, and a reminder you cannot see is not a reminder.

must_fit.source: Shelf to the underside of the cupboard above, measured with the lid's swing in mind.

temp_max_c.source: Steam from a shower, not direct heat.

environment.humidity: Intermittently high. Nothing here is moisture-sensitive, but the sensor's vents must not be blocked.

range_target_m.source: Distance from the bathroom shelf to the nearest Zigbee router.
range_target_m.how_to_close: Range-test in place: sensor inside the closed printed box, on the actual shelf, through the actual walls. Not on the desk next to the coordinator.

interactions.notes: The lid IS the interaction. Opening it is the only input the system has.

non_goals: It does not dispense, count or withhold medication. It watches a lid.
No display and no on-device alerting. The nagging happens on a phone.
No firmware of any kind. Adding an MCU here would add a battery to charge, a rail to budget and a bring-up to do, in exchange for nothing the vendor sensor does not already provide.
